text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- President Jacques Chirac reaffirms in a television address his committment to meeting the Maastricht treaty criteria on time for the planned switch to a european single currency, warns Prime Minister Lionel Jospin not to increase mandatory contributions, urges him to go ahead with privatisations. (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, Liberation).

-- Prime Minister Lionel Jospin announced Friday night he was halting the privatisation process of defence electronics group Thomson-CSF prepared by the previous government, said the state would keep a decisive stake in a new French defence electronics group to be formed around Thomson-CSF. (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, Liberation).
-- A new French defence electronics pillar around Thomson-CSF may take the form of an alliance with Alcatel-Alsthom, Dassault and Aerospatiale .

-- Luxury goods group LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault to outline to Guinness and GrandMet this week his counter-proposal to their merger project, which is expected to call for a three-way alliance in spirits sector.
-- Thomson-CSF may ally with missile and satellite activity of Aerospatiale.
-- Credit Lyonnais expected to announce sale of subsidiary Credit Lyonnais Portugal, as well as that of Italian subsidiary Credito Bergamasco and Irish subsidiary Woodchester.
-- Government vows to bring down to zero the forecast Social Security deficit for 1998.
-- LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault may consider selling Hennessy to Guinness in exchange for a 34 percent stake held by Guinness in champagne activity.
-- President Jacques Chirac vows to steer France on the path to monetary union.
-- State to pay back some 90 billion francs tomorrow to holders of bonds issued in 1993 at the initiative of Prime Minister Edouard Balladur.
-- OECD calls for higher investment in training and notably apprenticeship to help reduce unemployment.
-- Lagardere protests reports saying its rival Alcatel-Alsthom would be given an important role in a new group that may be formed around Thomson-CSF, calls them rumours.
